chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Ri'ab from al-Hasan al-Attar from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

When the pilgrim reaches 'Arafat before the rising of the dawn, then turns back from 'Arafat, and does not catch the people at Jam', and finds that they have already proceeded (to Muna), then he should stand for a short while at al-Mash'ar al-Haram and join the people at Muna, and there is no penalty upon him.

key_terms.أَفَاضُوا: They proceeded/flowed out (referring to the movement of pilgrims)
key_terms.الْمَشْعَرِ الْحَرَامِ: Al-Mash'ar al-Haram, the Sacred Mound (Mount Arafat's small mound)
key_terms.جَمْعٍ: Jam', the second station of Hajj where pilgrims gather after leaving 'Arafat
key_terms.عَرَفَاتٍ: 'Arafat, the plain where the main standing of Hajj occurs
key_terms.مِنًى: Muna, the valley where pilgrims spend the days of Tashriq
key_terms.وَلَا شَيْءَ عَلَيْهِ: And there is no penalty/dam upon him (exemption from penalty)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a pilgrim who leaves 'Arafat before dawn and misses the crowd at Jam'?
ai.summary: In al-Istibsar, Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling from Imam al-Sadi' (AS) addressing the specific scenario of a pilgrim who departs 'Arafat before dawn but misses the main congregation at Jam' al-Thani. The Imam clarifies that such a pilgrim is exempt from penalty (la shay'a 'alayhi) provided they perform a brief standing at al-Mash'ar al-Haram before joining the crowd in Muna, highlighting the flexibility in Hajj rituals when congregational timing is missed. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on the intention and essential acts over rigid adherence to group timing when circumstances prevent it.
